paper.title_en: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices
paper.abstract_en: Flat bands support compact localized states (CLSs), whereas bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain spatially localized despite having energies embedded in the continuum of extended states. Here, we investigate the connection between these phenomena in a class of one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices whose Bloch Hamiltonians take the pseudospin form H(k)=d(k)S. For integer pseudospin, the Hamiltonian intrinsically supports a zero-energy flat band and its associated compact localized states. When the effective pseudospin field has real transverse components and a purely imaginary longitudinal component, increasing non-Hermiticity compresses the dispersive bands toward the intrinsic zero-energy flat band, enabling their spectral overlap within a finite parameter range. The CLSs thus become embedded in the dispersive continuum and emerge as BICs. Adding a momentum-dependent Hermitian component along the gain-loss direction generally removes this spectral overlap without destroying the CLSs. We further extend this spectral mechanism to integer-pseudospin-n systems. These findings establish a connection between intrinsic flat-band localization and BIC formation through non-Hermitian spectral reconstruction.
